title: New here, looking for anti-pushback on using AI to create mods / game content / games
author: ContactIcy3963
selftext:
I am looking for feedback/justification to utilize AI tools to assist in the coding of video game mods, and eventually new game development itself. It’s pretty stigmatized but a lot of the low level code on open source / decompilable games AI can handle without breaking a sweat.

So far I’ve limited my scope to updating deprecated mods that were either abandoned or no longer regularly worked on by the modders so old mods for Minecraft, Balatro, 2d Pokemon, stellaris etc. AI has been able to update the mod to be workable to the most recent versions, and it’s been a blast getting it to work this way.

Course, I sometimes get flamed for the use of ANY AI here but I feel that this is right up its alley. I went from staring at long forgotten mods praying for an update to updating, and even enhancing, them myself. Y’all get similar sentiments, and how best to address them?

I’d like to eventually create my own game concepts but haven’t had much success with getting acceptable art assets. Any suggestions on how to improve image generation and where I should intervene with my own designs?

Thanks in advance for your feedback.

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: Photobashing used to get so much hate when come out. Now look it's common place. Mocap was the end of the animation companies... Instead it created new piple lines and jobs. And yes there was still loss of jobs. Marvel rivals is using ai in their stuff and it hasn't stopped people from playing it.   Ut they still haven't marked themselves using ai in their steam page. So that that how you want.

replies.author: ContactIcy3963
replies.body: Use of AI just raises the standard for those who use AI, which will naturally cause people who use AI to supersede the people who don’t.

comments.author: kosimus
comments.body:
There are fanatics out there who are staunchly against any use of generative AI whatsoever. They just see black and white, with no shades of grey. Those are the folks you'd be trying to convince, and it would be fruitless. Fanatics won't be convinced, because fanaticism cannot be reasoned with. And I think that's fine :).

I know it doesn't really answer your question, but that's what I think about it. 

Also, if making a prediction is permitted: they will always be out there, though in steadily decreasing numbers over time. Eventually no-AI development will be like making artisan soaps. Kinda cool for connoisseurs, but it won't shape the mass market. 

AI is used heavily in game development these days - by artists, coders, designers, PMs, and so on. I know it, because I've been working in the industry for nearly two decades by now. If a company in 2026 says they're not using AI, that is a lie. I can't help but feel like AI haters are either detached from reality, have only ever worked for very tiny projects, or have not been a part of a commercial gamedev enterprise within the last few years.  
What practically matters already now in commercial products is the ultimate quality of the release rather than tools used to make that release. If AI helped, that's great - you used that tool well. If AI broke it - you did not use it correctly.

So again - my advice is don't bother, it will be much healthier for you :).

replies.author: ContactIcy3963
replies.body:
Funny to see them rage over AI being used to simply audit existing code written by hobbyists, finding a ton of bugs, and revising the code to be compatible with current builds of a game. All time they want to do by hand? Which can be instead used for content generation? Not at all sorry codex did the work in 29 minutes that they couldn’t do in year. 

I work in finance myself so all the macros we wrote by hand got the AI treatment, and you know what? Even if it was my code, I was happy to get it improved by AI. I’m all the more better for it and many of the processes have either now run faster or become automated further so I can work on this hobby LUL. 

I get the whole destruction of entry level jobs and big wig corpo overly pushing AI, often in incorrect directions. But this technology will broaden the base of entrepreneurs who can become their own consulting firms and find niches every which way.

replies.author: minicoman
replies.body: Im a traditional artist, with 3d modeling,  and programming experience. Been doing game dev for 10+ years and Ai does not phase me one bit. Make what ever you want how ever you want. Forget about the criticism and let your full vision speak for itself. We cannot forget that we're a species of evolution and just because some mediums are enhanced doesn't mean others will be gone forever. Not everyone has the aptitude for certain things in life. So do the best that you can with what you can. The rest is just noise.

comments.author: Ok-File-2759
comments.body: As long as you use it as a tool and don’t just plan on one shot promoting your game and using the first thing it gives you, it’s not “AI slop”. Ignore the people that have AI paranoia. AI is the most powerful technology we’ve ever created and we’re the early adopters of it. Everyone else will catch on once it becomes the norm. Revolutionary technology always gets backlash at first
